citations.quote:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite subset of a positive $q$-Hadamard-lacunary sequence.
It is a union of finitely many sets $\Lambda_1,\ldots,\Lambda_r$, with each
successive ratio in $\Lambda_\nu$ at least $3$. For arbitrary unimodular
$\varepsilon_\lambda$ and each class, the Riesz product

$$P_\nu(x)=\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda_\nu}\left(1+\operatorname{Re}(\varepsilon_\lambda e_\lambda(x))\right)$$

is nonnegative, has integral $1$, and satisfies
$\widehat P_\nu(-\lambda)=\overline{\varepsilon_\lambda}/2$ for
$\lambda\in\Lambda_\nu$.

The lacunary and additive conventions are those of
[[def-hadamard-lacunary-sequence-and-lacunary-trigonometric-series]] and
[[lem-hadamard-gaps-bound-additive-representations]].

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

Set $Q=q^r$ and split the original indices of $\Lambda$ into $r$ residue classes $\Lambda_
u$. Each class has successive ratios at least $Q\ge3$. Set $\varepsilon_\lambda=a_\lambda/|a_\lambda|$ when $a_\lambda
e0$, and set it to $1$ otherwise. By [L1], the product $P_
u=\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda_
u}(1+\operatorname{Re}(\varepsilon_\lambda e_\lambda))$ is nonnegative, has integral one, and has the prescribed coefficients on its class. Empty classes use the product $1$.

Every nonzero frequency $m$ in the product expansion is a signed sum of distinct frequencies of $\Lambda_
u$. If $L$ is its largest contributing frequency, the sum of the smaller frequencies is less than $L/(Q-1)$, so $$ igl||m|-L igr|< rac{L}{Q-1}<\left(1- rac1qight)L.$$ Every other frequency of the original sequence is at most $L/q$ or at least $qL$; in the latter case its distance from $L$ is at least $(q-1)L>(1-1/q)L$. Thus if $|m|$ belongs to the original sequence it must equal $L$, which lies in this class. In particular $\widehat P_
u(-\lambda)=0$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda\setminus\Lambda_
u$.

Finite character integration, [L1], and this vanishing give $$\int_0^1F P_
u= rac12\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_
u}|a_\lambda|.$$ For completeness, if $z=\int F P_
u
e0$, multiplication by $\overline z/|z|$ and taking real parts gives $|z|\le\int |F|P_
u$; the same inequality is immediate if $z=0$. Apply [L2] to the real functions $|F|$ and $P_
u$ to obtain $$ rac12\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_
u}|a_\lambda|\le\int_0^1|F|P_
u\le\|F\|_\infty.$$

Summing over the $r$ classes yields $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}|a_\lambda|\le2r\|F\|_\infty$. The constant depends only on $q$ and $r$, not on the finite support or coefficients, so this is the Sidon inequality.
